research_question: In children and adolescents (aged 0–19 years) with overweight or obesity, what is the effect of digital health / technology-driven or technology-assisted interventions added to conventional care, compared with conventional care alone, on waist circumference (cm) at end of study?
treatment_label: Digital health / technology-assisted intervention plus conventional care
outcome_description: Waist circumference measured in centimetres at the end of the intervention/study period (including waist circumference z-score or percentile where reported as the study's waist measure) in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g means the technology-assisted intervention added to conventional care produced a greater reduction in waist circumference (smaller waist circumference) than conventional care alone.
search_queries: digital health intervention childhood obesity waist circumference randomized trial
mHealth app adolescent overweight weight management controlled trial anthropometric outcomes
telehealth exergame internet-based program pediatric obesity waist circumference effect
inclusion_criteria: Participants are children or adolescents aged 0–19 years with overweight or obesity (or a weight-management population including such youth)

Study evaluates any digital, technology-driven or technology-assisted component (app, website, SMS, telehealth, wearable, exergame, social media, e-learning) delivered alongside or as an addition to usual/conventional care, compared with a control group receiving conventional care or no digital component
Reports quantitative waist circumference (or waist-related anthropometric) data at end of study, or data sufficient to compute an effect size
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between a treatment condition and a control/comparison condition (single-arm or pre-post only designs without a control group)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no means with SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. adults only, no technology component, or no weight/anthropometric outcome)
moderators_to_extract: Type of digital technology (app, web, SMS, telehealth, wearable, exergame)
Mean participant age or age group (child vs adolescent)
